picks.title: Google launches Lyria 3.5 in the Gemini app, AI Studio and Gemini API
picks.headline: Google launches Lyria 3.5 in the Gemini app, AI Studio and Gemini API
picks.excerpt: Google has released Lyria 3.5, its best-sounding music generation model yet, now available in the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and the Gemini API. It brings more expressive vocals, richer arrangements and full-length song structure with SynthID watermarking on every track.
picks.rationale: A flagship model refresh from the biggest platform player, shipped simultaneously into three surfaces with SynthID baked in — the most directly usable release in the pool.

picks.title: Australia's ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from its official charts
picks.headline: Australia's ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from its official charts
picks.excerpt: Australia's ARIA has joined more than 20 countries in barring fully AI-generated songs from its official charts, though AI can still assist with sound design and arrangement if humans handle songwriting, lead vocals and primary instruments.
picks.rationale: A national chart body drawing the exact line between AI-assisted and AI-authored work shows where the industry-wide policy consensus is settling.

picks.title: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
picks.headline: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
picks.excerpt: Billboard has committed to identifying songs on its charts that were made with AI, setting out how it will flag AI involvement rather than exclude it outright, putting a disclosure standard on the industry's most-watched scoreboard.
picks.rationale: The industry's most-watched scoreboard choosing disclosure over exclusion sets a middle-path precedent other platforms will be measured against.

picks.title: FL Studio says GenAI can help people 'get into music-making'
picks.headline: FL Studio says GenAI can help people 'get into music-making'
picks.excerpt: Generative-AI music tools can be a powerful funnel for bringing complete beginners into human music-making, according to the CEO and CTO of Image-Line, the company behind DAW FL Studio, who frame prompt tools as an on-ramp to the DAW rather than a replacement for it.
picks.rationale: A major DAW maker publicly positioning prompt tools as a funnel rather than a threat is a rare vendor stance that reframes how producers should read GenAI adoption.
